name: @kruddage/editor
description: The KRUDD editor as a TypeScript application: a React app that consumes @kruddage/engine's WASM artifact and drives it. The first package in this workspace with third-party dependencies.
//engines: Higher than the workspace's >=20.11 floor, and it is Vite's floor rather than a preference of ours. Vite 8 drops Node 20.0-20.18. Nothing else here needs it, and if Vite ever goes this can go with it.
//exports: An application, not a library — so what it offers another package is where its build output landed, and nothing else. @kruddage/site needs that to stage the editor beside the shell, and the boundary check requires it to ask through this map rather than joining a relative path. The app itself is not reachable from here and is not meant to be.

scripts.//typecheck: Two configs, two invocations. tsconfig.json is the app and has no Node types; tsconfig.node.json is the build plugin, the scripts and the configs, and has them. Running only one would leave half the package unchecked, which is why `build` calls this rather than tsc directly.
scripts.//test: Vitest only. The browser suite is test:e2e, deliberately not wired into this script: `pnpm test` at the root runs in CI's workspace job, which has no emsdk and therefore no WASM for a browser to boot. See README.md, 'How this is tested' (#944, Q6).

//dependencies: @kruddage/engine is a devDependency, not a dependency, and the distinction is load-bearing: it is consulted by the build and the dev server to locate artifacts, and none of it is bundled into the shipped editor. Every entry above has a one-line justification in README.md — that list is the whole of the permission to add more.
